title: Stale locality affinity matrix caused canary amplification and cross-tier misrouting - postmortem
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: On 2025-02-12 a canary rollout for a minor routing policy change unexpectedly amplified and produced a global spike of fallback traffic to lower-tier model variants, increasing token latency and error rates for some customers. The control plane routed an outsized fraction of traffic to a small set of canary-capable regional pools due to a stale locality affinity matrix cached in the routing controller. Those pools hit soft limits, triggered autoscale backoff, and caused cross-tier fallbacks that cascaded through the routing tiers. This postmortem documents timeline, root cause, mitigations, and long-term fixes.
timeline:
2025-02-12T09:13Z: Canary rollout started for routing-policy v8.
2025-02-12T09:18Z: Observability alert - per-region request skew detected (10x expected variance).
2025-02-12T09:22Z: Canary region pools began returning 429/503 due to soft quota exhaustion.
2025-02-12T09:24Z: Tier routing engine began activating fallback variants globally.
2025-02-12T09:30Z: On-call routed traffic to fallback-safe regions and rolled back routing-policy v8.
2025-02-12T09:45Z: Emergency affinity refresh forced; skew reduced.
2025-02-12T10:10Z: Incident declared over; monitoring kept in heightened mode for 48h.
root_cause: A locality affinity matrix used by the routing controller was served from a cache with a TTL misconfiguration (24h) while the control plane expected near-real-time updates. During a canary rollout the new policy included a region affinity delta which should have rebalanced traffic, but the controller was applying an out-of-date affinity matrix. The mismatch led to concentrated routing to canary-capable pools. Contributing factors: 1) TTL misalignment between control-plane config publisher and routing controller cache, 2) lack of telemetry that verifies top-k region distribution against intended affinity, 3) autoscale soft-quota thresholds that are too conservative for canary bursts, and 4) fallback selection logic that aggressively falls back to lower-cost variants without progressive rate limiting.
impact_details:
Duration: ~1h  - 09:18Z to 10:30Z.
Customer-facing effects: elevated latencies (+200-800ms P95 for affected routes), increased 429/503 rates for ~4% of active API keys, and a spike in lower-tier model invocations resulting in degraded output quality for some users. Internal impact: paging of on-call SREs and mitigation time cost (~7 engineer-hours).
Estimated cost impact: small but non-trivial due to emergency autoscale bursts and additional fallback load; we estimate a one-off delta of ~$6k for that window.
immediate_mitigation_taken:
1) Rolled back routing-policy v8 to v7 across regions.
2) Forced a full affinity matrix refresh on all routing controllers (control-plane command: /admin/affinity/refresh).
3) Temporarily relaxed autoscale soft-quota thresholds for the overloaded pools to allow graceful absorption while scaling.
4) Added a short-term guard that throttles global fallbacks to <5% of total traffic to prevent cascade amplification.
long_term_fixes:
1) Change: Align TTL propagation - routing controller cache TTL reduced to 30s and control-plane publishes a monotonic config version stamp.
2) Add: Affinity checksum and config-version verification; controllers reject stale matrices with log+metric emission.
3) Observability: Implement 'region skew' SLO and alert that triggers when any region exceeds expected routing proportion by >3x.
4) Autoscale: Review and increase soft-quota headroom for canary-capable pools and add burst budget for controlled canary spikes.
5) Routing policy: Implement progressive rollouts with traffic steering ramp (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) and circuit-breaker that pauses ramp on region imbalance.
6) Fallback logic: Introduce progressive fallback ramp and per-customer impact scoring to avoid global aggressive fallbacks.

- ENG: Implement TTL/config-version enforcement in routing controller (owner: Marco Rivera) - due 2025-03-07.
- SRE: Tune autoscale soft-quotas and add burst budget primitives (owner: Priya Nair) - due 2025-02-28.
- Observability: Add region-skew alert and dashboard (owner: Lee Chen) - due 2025-02-24.
- PM: Update rollout playbook to require progressive ramping for policy changes that touch affinity matrix (owner: Nora Kim) - due 2025-03-01.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-25102: Add config-version handshake to routing-controller startup
ENG-25103: Add unit + integration tests for affinity acceptance/rejection
ENG-25210: Implement progressive rollout gating in the console
lessons_learned:
- Assume caches can be stale; design control-plane interactions to be explicit about versioning.
- Canary logic must include distribution checks (not just health checks) to catch skew early.
- Fallbacks need rate-limiting and customer-aware policies to avoid quality regressions at scale.
- Observability should include invariants (region distribution, per-tier fallback rate) that fail early and loudly.
communication: Incident post sent to #sre and #routing on 2025-02-13 with TLDR, root cause, and action items. Confluence write-up: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/ENG-25017+Stale+Affinity+Postmortem. Status email to affected customers sent 2025-02-14 by Customer Success. Internal retro held 2025-02-18; notes linked below.
review_feedback:
PM Nora: Ensure console rollout UI enforces ramp steps for policies that touch affinity.
Design Lee: dashboard should surface per-model variant fallback rate alongside region distribution.
SRE Priya: autoscale thresholds require simulation tests; create a synthetic traffic test harness for canary bursts.
Engineering: add a canary acceptance gate that validates region distribution before allowing >5% traffic to new policy.
status_notes: All long-term items have owners and deadlines; ENG TTL enforcement PR merged 2025-02-19 (runtime-1.18). Observability alerting merged 2025-02-22. Close monitoring window ended 2025-03-04.
